title: 3.2%追平纪录：本十年末或到4%，为何2029年才转折？
speaker: Tony Crescenzi

segments.en: I refer to the interest payments often when people ask about the government debt and they do very often.
segments.zh: 当人们问起政府债务时，我经常提到利息支付，他们确实也经常问。

segments.en: I like what I try to refer to the current situation is as a read my lips moment, now let me explain it.
segments.zh: 我喜欢把当前局势称为“读我的唇”时刻，让我解释一下。

segments.en: In 1988, George Bush has candidate at the convention in a speech written by Peggy Noonan who wrote speeches from Ronald Reagan. She said the biggest takeaway from the convention is when George Bush said, read my lips, no new taxes.
segments.zh: 1988年，乔治·布什作为候选人在大会上发表由佩吉·努南撰写的演讲，她曾为罗纳德·里根写稿。她说大会最大的亮点是布什说：“读我的唇，不加新税。”

segments.en: 1990, as president, George Bush raised taxes and nathmath to the Republican Party, typically doesn't raise taxes.
segments.zh: 1990年，作为总统，乔治·布什加税了，这对通常不加税的共和党来说很不寻常。

segments.en: Because the interest on the debt reached a record level back then, 3.2% of GDP. So that trillion dollars, David, that you mentioned, is 3.2% of GDP.
segments.zh: 因为当时债务利息达到创纪录水平，占GDP的3.2%。所以你提到的那1万亿美元，大卫，就是GDP的3.2%。

segments.en: So we're back to that level for the first time likely to reach 4% by the end of the decade.
segments.zh: 所以我们首次回到那个水平，到本十年末可能达到4%。

segments.en: So the read my lips moment is in 2029, when a president has to do something that's in nathma to his or her party, one final note on it, Bill Clinton did as well.
segments.zh: 所以“读我的唇”时刻在2029年，届时总统必须做一些对其政党来说不寻常的事，最后一点，比尔·克林顿也这么做了。

segments.en: He cut the capital gains tax rate, even though raised the top tax rate, but it's been fluctuating for 40 years in the high thirties, no big deal, really.
segments.zh: 他降低了资本利得税率，尽管提高了最高税率，但40年来一直在30%多的高位波动，其实没什么大不了的。

segments.en: So he did something in nathma to the party. The actions by those two presidents led to four years of budget surpluses eventually by the end of the 1990s.
segments.zh: 所以他做了对其政党不寻常的事。这两位总统的行动最终在90年代末带来了四年的预算盈余。

segments.en: So we need a president in a read my lips moment in 2029, when taking office, to do something different than the party might expect, because this is the only way to tackle this problem, to do something unusual.
segments.zh: 所以我们需要一位总统在2029年上任时迎来“读我的唇”时刻，做一些政党可能意想不到的事，因为这是解决这个问题的唯一途径，做一些不寻常的事。

segments.en: But it's such a policy conundrum, right? Because you don't want to be someone who's raising taxes on your donors, on your investors, you don't want to be seen as stunting growth through the market.
segments.zh: 但这是一个政策难题，对吧？因为你不想成为对捐助者、对投资者加税的人，你不想被视为通过市场阻碍增长。

segments.en: But at the same time, you're getting to a point where this in itself could stunt the market, it is starting to hurt financial products that is starting to make a difference. Because in the end, it's sapping money away from the private sector. It's raising borrowing costs.
segments.zh: 但与此同时，你正达到一个临界点，这本身可能阻碍市场，开始伤害金融产品，开始产生影响。因为最终，它正在抽走私营部门的资金。它在提高借贷成本。
